item.title: Amplifying Early Career Researchers' Voices for Gender and Inclusive Equality
item.content:encoded:
Anne-Sophie Godfroy, Université Paris-Est Créteil

Victoria Showunmi, University College London

Ama Lawani, University of Stirling

Peliwe Mnguni, UNISA Graduate School of Business Leadership

Afifa Knanam, Lahore College for Women University

Early Career Researchers face increasingly precarious employment conditions, with these challenges shaped significantly by gender. While women comprise nearly half of doctoral graduates in Europe, they remain underrepresented in certain fields and disproportionately occupy insecure positions. Beyond gender, intersecting factors like race, disability, and socioeconomic status create multiple barriers to career progression.

This special issue amplifies ECRs' voices by examining their experiences through gendered and intersectional lenses. It highlights structural inequalities in academia, challenges traditional research career concepts, and proposes institutional changes to address sexism. The issue invites research on gender equality initiatives, academic mobility, inclusive leadership, and frameworks for evaluating gender equality policies.

The call welcomes diverse contributions from ECRs and underrepresented researchers, including empirical studies, case studies, policy analyses, and personal reflections addressing the key thematic areas, with emphasis on improving working conditions and career prospects in academic institutions.

Appel publié par Gender Work and Organization. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Gender Equality in Career Prospects and Working Conditions at Early Career Stages
  • The Gendered Impact of Mobility and Migration
  • Integrating ECRs into Decision-Making Processes
  • Intersectional Analysis of Inequalities
  • Monitoring and Evaluating Gender Equality Policies
  • Critical reflections on gender equity and its contemporary resistance in organizational settings and media ecosystems
  • How leaders and organizations engage with gender issues through activism, partnerships, internal policies, and public critique
  • Intersectional perspectives on gender, race, class, and sexuality and the dynamics of progress and regression
  • How gender biases are addressed and produced in the realms of innovation, tech, and entrepreneurship
  • Analyzing gender inequality and its stagnation in workforce participation, compensation, and promotion opportunities
  • Gender fluidity and non-binary representations in the corporate world and organizational practices
  • Examining ethical and sustainable practices through a gender lens to address inclusivity in environmental and social initiatives
  • Empirical studies addressing gender and equality in academia, with particular attention to gender, mobility, and precarious employment conditions
  • Case studies highlighting gender equality initiatives in academic and research institutions
  • Policy recommendations and critical analysis of gender-sensitive recruitment, evaluation, and career development practices in academia
  • Innovative solutions aimed at reducing gender-based violence and fostering safer, more inclusive environments for women and marginalized groups within academic settings
  • Methodologies for monitoring and evaluating the impact of gender equality measures
  • Theoretical interventions exploring concepts of gender, equality, and academic structures
  • Autoethnographies reflecting on personal experiences related to gender and academic life
  • Practitioner reflections offering insights from those actively engaged in promoting gender equality in academic contexts
  • Interdisciplinary dialogue fostering collaboration and knowledge exchange across fields to advance gender equality in research and academia

Timeline

  • May 15, 2026: Deadline for optional 250-word abstract submission via email to receive initial feedback
  • July 1, 2026: Online developmental webinar to provide feedback on abstracts
  • October 31, 2026: Full paper submission deadline

item.title: All About En-During Crisis? "Other Stories" of Women Entrepreneurs
item.content:encoded:
Jasmine Jaim, Jahangirnagar University

Huriye Yeröz, De Montfort University

Bronwyn Wood, United Arab Emirates University

This special issue challenges the predominant narrative in scholarship on women entrepreneurs facing crises, which typically emphasizes their vulnerabilities and capacity to endure hardship. Instead, the call invites research that positions women entrepreneurs as active agents driving meaningful change across individual, familial, community, regional, national, and global levels.

The special issue seeks contributions examining both the positive and negative dimensions of entrepreneurship during crises, spanning the crisis period itself as well as pre- and post-crisis contexts. It aims to advance understanding of how gender intersects with entrepreneurship and crisis experiences, filling gaps in existing theory, empirical knowledge, and policy recommendations.

Appel publié par Gender Work and Organization. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Crisis and entrepreneurial or societal opportunities
  • Crisis and women entrepreneurs' identities, strengths and strategies
  • Crisis and women entrepreneurs' contributions to society
  • Crisis and a more gender equitable society through women's entrepreneurship
  • Post-Crisis and women entrepreneurs in peacebuilding and regeneration
  • Post-Crisis and impact of resilience
  • Post-Crisis and women entrepreneurs' better work-life balance, improved wellbeing concern and healthier relationships with employees
  • Crises, women's entrepreneurship and power relations
  • Crisis and dark sides of women's entrepreneurship
  • Women's entrepreneurship, crises, and entrepreneurial eco-systems
  • Women's entrepreneurship, crises, and other-than-humans
  • Women's entrepreneurship, crises and entrepreneurial education
  • Women's entrepreneurship, crises, and feminist perspectives

item.title: Change Meets Resistance: Re(shaping) Gender Dynamics in an Era of Backlash
item.content:encoded:
Elena Cedrola, Macerata University

Cinzia Colapinto, Venice School of Management

Lauren Gurrieri, RMIT University

Stefania Masè, IPAG Business School

Alisa Minina Jeunemaître, Emlyon Business School

Shumaila Yousafzai, Nazarbayev University

While some countries have advanced gender equality, many now experience significant backlash undermining this progress. Recent developments include government policy shifts limiting gender recognition, major corporations scaling back diversity initiatives, and the rise of online movements promoting traditional gender roles alongside broader polarization around diversity and inclusion policies.

This special issue examines how gender issues are negotiated and contested across organizations, markets, and society. It brings together fragmented research on intersections of gender with leadership, labor, media, and consumer experiences, exploring how corporate engagement with gender equity generates support and backlash while raising questions about authenticity and performativity.

Appel publié par Gender Work and Organization. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Critical reflections on gender equity and its contemporary resistance in organizational settings and media ecosystems
  • How leaders and organizations engage with gender issues (and associated backlash) through activism, partnerships, internal policies, and public critique
  • Intersectional perspectives on gender, race, class, and sexuality and the dynamics of progress and regression
  • How gender biases are (re)addressed and (re)produced in the realms of innovation, tech, and entrepreneurship
  • Analyzing gender inequality and its stagnation in workforce participation, compensation, and promotion opportunities
  • Gender fluidity and non-binary representations in the corporate world and organizational practices, and the implications of their political reception
  • Examining ethical and sustainable practices through a gender lens to address inclusivity in environmental and social initiatives
  • Exploring non-western perspectives and representations of diversity, equity and inclusion and backlash
  • How gender identities (feminine, masculine, non-binary, and trans) are constructed, challenged, or reinforced across media, advertising, and popular culture
  • How stereotypical gender roles are being reimagined, revived, or resisted in contemporary branding, media, and organizational discourse
  • What social, cultural, or emotional forces shape the renewed appeal of stereotypical femininities and masculinities in contemporary consumer and organizational life
  • What narratives, rituals, or aesthetic strategies are used to communicate shifting gender dynamics, and how are they received across different cultural and generational contexts

Timeline

  • October 31, 2026: Submission Deadline

item.title: Further Locating Masculinities in Gender, Work and Organisational Contexts
item.content:encoded:
Andreas Giazitzoglu, Northumbria University

Miruna Radu-Lefebvre, Audencia Business School

Jason Luger, Northumbria University

Callum Kimpton, Monash University

Kai Roland Green, Aarhus University

Garth Stahl, The University of Queensland

Masculinities studies has expanded significantly across disciplines and emerging contexts including entrepreneurship, healthcare, education, and politics. Recent scholarship increasingly adopts constructivist, decolonial, and intersectional approaches to understand how men enact masculine identities at work. This special issue invites contributions that deepen understanding of how gender shapes social arrangements and well-being in contemporary work and organisational contexts.

Gender, Work & Organization has become a leading venue for empirical masculinities scholarship. Recent contributions demonstrate how masculinities relate to inclusion and exclusion in workplaces, how they are shaped by organisational spaces and professional socialisation, and how individuals are marginalised when they fail to conform to masculine norms. The journal seeks further analysis exploring these complex relationships between gender, power, hierarchy, and organisational dynamics.

Appel publié par Gender Work and Organization. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Changing imaginaries of bodies and body types in work and organisational settings (e.g., the role of muscularity, body-art and digital representations of the body)
  • New and emergent forms of 'masculine capital' in work and organisations
  • How historical circumstances have impacted contemporary masculinities in work and organisations
  • The physical spaces of masculinity and how they impact work and organisations
  • Global variegations and convergences in trends in both hegemonic and counter-hegemonic masculinities
  • Queer(ying) masculinities in work and organisations
  • Critical readings of images, discourses, politics and practices linked to masculinities in work and organisations
  • How masculinities are negotiated and shaped during early professional socialisation and how these processes inform the reproduction of gendered work and organisational cultures
  • What novel and innovative methodologies can be leveraged to advance the study of gendered power and practice in work and organisational settings?
  • What can the analysis of contemporary workplaces (remote, virtual and transnational) reveal about modern masculinities?
  • How are workplace and organisational masculinities re-shaped or reconstituted in response to emerging social and political pressures that threaten hegemonic gender orders?
  • How can symbolic dimensions of masculine practice advance our understanding of recognition and legitimacy in specific organisational fields?
  • How do portrayals of masculinities in media, culture and public discourse inform our understanding of gendered life and livelihoods?

Timeline

  • January 10, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Gender and Professional Sports: Intersectional Perspectives
item.content:encoded:
Roman Gibel, University of Zürich

Edeltraud Hanappi-Egger, Vienna University of Business and Economics

Anett Hermann, Vienna University of Business and Economics

Georgios Tsourvakas, National and Kapodistrian University Athens

Natasha Winkler-Titus, Stellenbosch Business School

This special issue examines how gender shapes professional sports organizations and the experiences of those within them. It draws on feminist and intersectional frameworks to understand how power dynamics, organizational structures, and institutional policies create gendered hierarchies that affect athletes, coaches, and administrators. The issue also considers how race, class, sexuality, and other identities compound gender-based inequalities in sports.

The special issue welcomes interdisciplinary research that connects gender and sports to broader questions in work, organization, and management. Submissions should employ diverse methodologies and advance both theoretical and empirical knowledge, exploring themes such as career trajectories, leadership, economic structures, media representation, policy effects, and the specific challenges faced by transgender and non-binary athletes seeking inclusion in sports spaces.

Appel publié par Gender Work and Organization. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Gendered Labor and Career Trajectories in Professional Sports: In what ways are career paths, working conditions, and opportunities in professional sports shaped by gender, and how do these dynamics intersect with broader organizational and societal structures?
  • Organizational Dynamics and Gender: How do sports organizations reproduce or challenge gender norms? What are the implications of gendered leadership, policies, and practices within sports institutions?
  • Economic and Organizational Power Structures in Sports: How do economic and organizational power relations in professional sports reproduce or challenge gendered hierarchies, and what implications do they have for inclusion, leadership, and equity within sport institutions?
  • Intersectionality in Sports: How do race, class, sexuality, disability, and other social categories intersect with gender to shape experiences and inequalities in sports?
  • Gendered Experiences in Sports: How do gender identities influence participation, performance, and recognition in various sports? What are the lived experiences of athletes, coaches, and administrators across the gender spectrum?
  • Trans and Non-Binary Inclusion: How are trans and non-binary athletes navigating sports spaces? What challenges and opportunities exist for inclusive practices?
  • Media Representations and Gender: How are athletes and sports events gendered in media coverage? What impact do these representations have on public perceptions and gender norms?
  • Policy and Governance: What are the effects of policies related to gender equity, inclusion, and diversity in sports at local, national, and international levels?
  • International and Interdisciplinary Perspectives: How can international and interdisciplinary collaborations advance research on gender and sports, fostering more inclusive, diverse, and globally informed understandings of work and organization in sporting contexts?

Timeline

  • May 1, 2026: Paper Preparatory Workshop (online)
  • August 1, 2026: Open for Submissions
  • February 1, 2027: Submission Deadline

item.title: Gender, Work and Organization in the Balkans: Contemporary Challenges, Comparative Insights, and Theory-Building
item.content:encoded:
Natalia Vershinina, Audencia Business School

Amitabh Anand, Excelia Business School

Ivona Hideg, Saïd Business School, University of Oxford

Sanja Pekovic, University of Montenegro

Ivana Bulog, University of Split

Azra Bičo, International University of Sarajevo

Simona Kukovič, School of Advanced Social Studies & University of Ljubljana

The Western Balkans present a distinctive context for studying gender and work, combining labour-market gender gaps, high female inactivity, and informality with legacies of conflict and complex state-society relations. Women have played crucial roles in post-conflict recovery and civil society development, but existing global organizational theories inadequately capture these experiences and contributions.

This special issue seeks rigorous, comparative research that documents contemporary gendered labour dynamics in the region, theorizes how regional specificities—such as post-socialist transition, conflict legacies, and EU integration pressures—shape organizational practices and careers, and develops conceptual contributions relevant to global gender and organization scholarship. The issue particularly welcomes papers evaluating policy effectiveness and linking local practices to international regimes.

Appel publié par Gender Work and Organization. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Gendered labour markets, informality, care work, and self-employment in the Balkans
  • Gender pay inequality and organizational stratification
  • Gendered leadership, management, and corporate governance
  • Policy, Europeanization, and institutional change affecting gender equality
  • Flexible work, gig economy, and new forms of gendered work
  • Gender norms, education, and reproduction of inequality
  • Patriarchy, religion, and gendered organizational cultures
  • Urbanization, space, and gendered work practices

Timeline

  • December 1, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Gendered Practices at Work: (Un)intended Consequences Across Organizations and Markets
item.content:encoded:
Daniela Giménez-Jiménez, TU Dortmund

Magdalena Markowska, Umeå University

Patricia Gabaldón, IE University

Caren Scheepers, Gordon Institute of Business Science

This special issue examines how gendered practices are constructed and enacted within organizations, and what consequences they produce. While gender as social practice is theoretically accepted, understanding how these practices operate across different contexts remains limited. The issue addresses a critical gap: persistent structural inequalities continue to disadvantage women globally, yet equality initiatives sometimes produce unintended negative consequences such as reinforcing stereotypes.

The special issue welcomes diverse approaches examining both intended outcomes of gendered practices and unintended consequences. It seeks to understand how gendered practices at multiple levels are negotiated, resisted, and transformed across different industries and cultural contexts, particularly through feminist theories including intersectional and postcolonial perspectives.

Appel publié par Gender Work and Organization. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Does the (mis)use of gendered practices in organizations and industries affect various occupations?
  • How do women and men employees navigate gendered practices in women-dominated versus men-dominated industries? Are there differences across these industries?
  • Which specific gendered practices do women and which ones do men (mis)use, and what consequences do these have for organizational culture?
  • How are current discourses shaping gendered practices? Do these gendered practices influence organizational outcomes, outputs, or impacts?
  • How does the production, reproduction, and construction of gender affect business outcomes? Are the effects the same or different within and outside organisations?
  • How do gendered practices influence women's networks, particularly given unique challenges women and minorities face in creating personal networks in organizational contexts?
  • What are the consequences of women's programs on their networks, and what are the outcomes of these programs for women and men, as well as for organizations?
  • Who are the actors actively constructing, resisting and shaping gendered practices at the different levels? What conditions enable and which ones inhibit production, change, and use of gendered practices?
  • How does the portrayal of women and men in business—through media representations and policies—affect leadership stereotypes?
  • What roles do masculine and feminine voices play concerning gendered practices? Could individuals influence and confront gendered practices?
  • How do women with intersectional identities or social experiences—such as LGBTQIA++ individuals or female migrants—create, build, or construct new gendered practices?
  • In what ways do these practices influence organizations, industries, and markets?
  • How are gendered practices shaped within women- and men-dominated industries?

Timeline

  • January 31, 2027: Submission Deadline

item.title: Neurodiversity, Gender, and Work
item.content:encoded:
Sophie Hennekam, Audencia Business School

Bettina Lynda Bastian, American University in Bulgaria

Bruno Felix, Fundação Dom Cabral

This special issue explores how neurodiversity and gender intersect in workplace settings. Neurodivergent individuals possess valuable cognitive strengths but face significant employment challenges including high unemployment, discrimination, and limited career advancement, often due to neurotypical workplace norms.

Gender compounds these challenges, as neurodivergent women and gender-diverse individuals navigate both ableist expectations and societal gender norms. Diagnostic criteria biased toward male presentation result in underdiagnosis for other genders. Despite growing awareness of neurodiversity, organizational research remains limited, particularly regarding intersections with diverse gender identities.

The special issue invites empirical, conceptual, and practice-based research applying organizational theories to understand neurodivergent workers' experiences. It welcomes unconventional methodologies, interdisciplinary collaborations, and submissions from neurodivergent scholars, aiming to generate insights beneficial to both organizational practice and scholarship.

Appel publié par Gender Work and Organization. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Unique challenges and opportunities neurodivergent and gender-diverse individuals face in the workplace
  • Co-occurrence of multiple forms of neurodivergence and its impact on workplace experiences
  • Role of organizational culture, co-workers, and diversity policies in shaping experiences of neurodivergent individuals
  • How societal norms surrounding femininity affect workplace experiences of neurodivergent women
  • Intersection of neurodivergence with other marginalized identities
  • Insights from experiences of gender-diverse neurodivergent individuals regarding gender norms and identity expression
  • Participatory research methodologies that empower neurodivergent voices
  • Manifestation of stereotypes about neurodiversity differently for men and women in professional environments
  • Navigation of identities by non-binary or gender-diverse individuals within predominantly ableist workplaces
  • Role of cultural perceptions in shaping experiences of neurodivergent individuals across different genders
  • Organizational support for neurodivergent individuals and creation of inclusive climate at work, including HRM policies and practices
  • Coping strategies of neurodivergent individuals and gender differences in coping
  • Identity management strategies and gender disclosure decisions of gender-diverse neurodivergent individuals at work

item.title: Reconfiguring the Global Politics of Care: Actors, Transformations and Policy Alternatives
item.content:encoded:
Elifcan Celebi, University of Oxford

Rossella Ciccia,

Ayşe Dursun, University of Vienna

David Palomera, University of Southern Denmark

The global care sector faces intensifying challenges from demographic changes, the pandemic, and fiscal constraints, resulting in overburdened systems and widening inequalities. Market-based and government responses have increasingly transformed care through commodification, financialisation, digitalization, and platformisation, with varied consequences across different regions and economies.

This special issue seeks empirical research exploring how care governance is being reshaped by economic, social, and technological changes, and how new political movements are mobilizing around care issues. The editors welcome studies using diverse methodologies and approaches—including feminist, intersectional, and postcolonial perspectives—that examine actors driving these transformations, institutional alternatives emerging across geographies, and policy innovations that might address the care crisis.

Appel publié par Gender Work and Organization. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How do ongoing processes of commodification, financialisation, digitalization and (in)formalisation transform care? What roles do markets and financial actors, as well as international organizations, governments, feminist movements, labour organisations, play?
  • How are new and old actors (such as care workers, social movements, care platforms, cooperatives, financial organisations, or public–private and public-communitarian partnerships) reshaping care infrastructures, practices, and labour across the Global North and Global South?
  • How are emerging social, economic and technological processes reconfiguring the relationship between states, markets, families, and communities in different contexts? How do gender, race, care, labour, and migration regimes become entangled in new or altered ways at global, national and local scales? And how do these processes affect gender, class, race, nation hierarchies and intersecting inequalities across caregivers and care receivers?
  • What kind of policy innovations offer promising alternatives to the structural crisis of care? Which proposals in diverse geographies (e.g., communitarian services, caring cities or care commons) from social movements, international organizations, experts, or local initiatives show promise to offer a pathway to a more caring society?

Timeline

  • April 1, 2026: Submissions open
  • October 30, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Special Issue Proposals
item.content:encoded:
Gender, Work & Organization seeks proposals for special issues to be published in 2026 and beyond. The journal is particularly interested in work that addresses urgent and underexplored questions at the intersection of gender, work, and organization, especially proposals that engage critically with feminist theory and bring diverse perspectives into conversation. Proposals from organizers of the GWO 2025 Conference are especially welcome, as are suggestions from emerging scholarly collaborations presenting innovative and boundary-pushing research aligned with the journal's mission.

The journal is seeking special issues that demonstrate strong editorial collaboration and clear strategies for ensuring inclusivity throughout the publication process, including in authorship, peer review, and the mentoring of early-career scholars. Proposals should include the issue title and theme, a clear rationale for the contribution to the field, a diverse editorial team with relevant experience, a realistic timeline, and a plan for outreach and promotion.

Appel publié par Gender Work and Organization. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Gender, work, and organization
  • Feminist theory, method, and praxis
  • Intersectional and post/decolonial perspectives
  • Underexplored questions in gender and organizational studies
  • Diverse geographies and voices in organizational research
  • Inclusivity in authorship, peer review, and mentoring of early career scholars

Timeline

  • December 31, 2025: Deadline for Special Issue proposals (with proposed manuscript deadline in 2026)
  • June 30, 2026: Deadline for Special Issue proposals (with proposed manuscript deadline in 2027)

item.title: The Gendered Architecture of Family Firms: Optics, Authority, Governance
item.content:encoded:
Natalia Vershinina, Audencia Business School

Cristina Bettinelli, University of Bergamo

Marco Mismetti, Stockholm School of Economics

Giovanna Campopiano, University of Bergamo

Paola Rovelli, Free University of Bozen-Bolzano

Andreas Giazitzoglu, Northumbria University

This special issue examines how gender inequality in family firms operates through organisational structures and decision-making processes rather than individual attitudes. The call challenges mainstream family business research that overlooks how patriarchal norms systematically advantage male family members while rendering women's contributions invisible or subordinate.

Contributions should apply gender theory and the willingness-ability-authority framework to show how governance structures enable or constrain efforts toward redistribution of power. The editors particularly welcome studies exposing how initiatives may appear progressive without achieving substantive change, and work examining hegemonic masculinity in family contexts—how ideals of the effective heir shape succession decisions and police gender performances.

Appel publié par Gender Work and Organization. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Hegemonic masculinities and succession: How are readiness, leadership potential and fit defined and performed in family firms? Which rites of passage, informal trials, and evaluation criteria enact masculinity contests among heirs? Under what discursive and relational conditions can men's explicit advocacy for equality enhance, rather than erode, their standing? When and how do care-centred, collaborative, or non-hegemonic masculinities gain legitimacy?
  • Willingness, ability, and the redistribution of authority: Where does willingness collapse under kinship politics, and where does it convert into action? Which specific instruments — binding remuneration committees, gender-equal succession clauses, mixed family/non-family appointment slates with veto power — shift ability from kin coalitions to institutionalised bodies with enforceable rights? How do these arrangements travel across generational transitions?
  • Emotional, aesthetic, and reputational glue work: How do feminised labours of harmony, client smoothing and reputational caretaking sustain legitimacy without converting into jurisdiction, ownership or promotion in family firms and in entrepreneurial families? What happens when these labours are surfaced, measured, rewarded, or redistributed, and what is the role of the family in this? How do these practices differentially tax daughters, wives, in-laws, and non-family managers?
  • Temporal dynamics: path dependence and rupture: When do equality reforms survive family firm succession events? What tipping points loosen masculinity-contest logics and allow successors to deploy formal authority for redistribution rather than preservation? How do market shocks, legal changes, or religious norms recalibrate both willingness and ability in family firms? How do successors' identity work when logics evolve during a generational transition?
  • Intersectional and comparative analysis: How do age, class, ethnicity, marital/parental status, sexual orientation, and religion shape the policing of masculinities, feminities and the credibility of actor's authority claims? How do family structures (extended families, polygamy, multi-branch ownership) mediate gendered governance? What travels, and what does not, across national cultures, legal frameworks, and faith traditions?
  • External accountability vs. internal decision rights: When do ESG disclosures, audits, and investor or customer pressures reconfigure internal masculine ideals and decision rights in family firms and when are they absorbed as optics? What coupling mechanisms translate external accountability into binding internal authority for equality actors?

Timeline

  • October 1, 2027: Submission deadline
